conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that the claim is supported, citing randomized phase III trial evidence (ZOE-70), FDA labeling, and CDC summaries showing high efficacy (91.3%) in reducing shingles among adults aged 70 years or older.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: the claim is supported, not false.** The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix) reduced confirmed shingles (herpes zoster) in adults aged **70 years or older** in randomized, placebo-controlled phase III evidence.

The key study, ZOE-70, randomly assigned adults ≥70 to two vaccine doses or placebo; the published trial concluded that the vaccine reduced risks of both shingles and post-herpetic neuralgia in this age group. The FDA labeling says efficacy in people ≥70 was assessed using a **pre-specified pooled analysis** of two studies. CDC summarizes the phase III trial program (>30,000 participants) as finding **91.3% efficacy against shingles** after more than three years among adults ≥70.

Important qualifications: this is relative efficacy under trial conditions and depends on completing the two-dose regimen; it does not mean zero vaccinated people develop shingles. The pivotal studies were funded by the manufacturer (GSK), but their randomized, placebo-controlled design and consistency with FDA/CDC assessments make the evidence strong. Thus, the evidence does not support the view that RZV fails to reduce shingles in this population.

Sources:  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/  
- https://www.fda.gov/media/108597/download  
- https://www.cdc.gov/pinkbook/hcp/table-of-contents/chapter-23-zoster.html
